A.explanation: The two surfaces cannot both shorten. Bending makes one side shorter and the opposite side longer.

B.explanation: The two surfaces cannot both stretch. Bending makes one side stretch and the opposite side squash.

C.explanation: The sagging centre squeezes the top surface X together and stretches the bottom surface Y apart, so X is in compression and Y is in tension.

D.explanation: This reverses the bending effect. The concave top is squashed, not stretched, and the convex bottom is stretched, not squashed.

hints: Look at the shape of the beam between the two pivots: the middle has sagged down so the top surface X is concave and the bottom surface Y is convex.
Recall that compression means layers are pushed together and shortened, while tension means layers are pulled apart and lengthened.
Compare the arc length of the inner concave side with the outer convex side at the centre to decide which of X and Y is squashed and which is stretched.
walkthrough: Identify the deformation from the diagram: the beam bends downward between the pivots, sagging in the middle under its weight.
State the rule for bending: the inside of a bend is forced into a shorter length and is in compression, while the outside of a bend is forced into a longer length and is in tension.
Apply this to the top surface X: it forms the inside of the sag, so its material is pushed together and shortened, which is compression.
Apply this to the bottom surface Y: it forms the outside of the sag, so its material is pulled apart and lengthened, which is tension.
Combine the two results: X is in compression and Y is in tension. This is option C.
